summary: Frontend (Expo web) testing of CardFlow finance app. App fails to initialize due to a CRITICAL expo-sqlite web error (SQLITE_MISUSE / Error code 21) occurring during DB schema setup, which short-circuits the entire AppDataContext refresh and renders an Expo red-screen overlay on top of the UI. Dashboard shell renders (testID dashboard-screen, dashboard-combined-limit, dashboard-msi-debt, 4 pie legends visible) but all values are $0.00 and tabs are intercepted by the error overlay so no further interactive flow (create card / MSI / income / expense / category / alert switch / persistence) could be exercised end-to-end on web.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught Error: 'Error code 21: bad parameter or other API misuse' from expo-sqlite/web/WorkerChannel.ts:64. Triggered on first DB init on web. AppDataProvider.refresh() then never resolves successfully; loading flag stays effectively in error state and Expo renders a red-screen overlay over the entire app. Removing 'PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL' on web (already applied as a defensive fix) did NOT resolve it, so the misuse is in another statement (likely the multi-statement execAsync CREATE TABLE block or the seed INSERT OR IGNORE on web sqlite-wasm).
'Activar' button is implemented as a Text with onPress; should be wrapped in TouchableOpacity/Pressable for proper 44x44 touch target and accessibility on mobile.

integration_issues.issue: DB init throws Error 21; UI cannot reach any interactive flow on web because the Expo error overlay blocks all clicks (tab buttons report not visible/clickable).

issues: Hero KPIs render correctly (Resumen title, mes en mayúsculas, combined limit, available today, end-of-month projection, 4-color pie legend) but show $0 due to DB failure — could not validate visual updates with real data.

react_native_issues.issue: props.pointerEvents deprecation warnings in console (use style.pointerEvents) — non-blocking but should be cleaned up

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL) the expo-sqlite Error 21 on web. Recommended steps: (1) Split the multi-statement execAsync schema into individual execAsync('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ...') calls (sqlite-wasm web is stricter about batched statements); (2) Wrap initSchema/seedDefaultCategories in try/catch and log the underlying SQL to surface the failing statement; (3) Verify INSERT OR IGNORE for default categories works on web (consider getFirstAsync+runAsync per row guard already used). Also surface the error in AppDataContext catch block instead of swallowing in finally so user sees a proper retry UI rather than Expo's red overlay.
After SQLite fix, re-run the full test suite (steps 1–10 in the request). The previous test attempt achieved only step 1 (dashboard shell) before being blocked.
Consider replacing 'Activar' Text+onPress in alertas.tsx with a TouchableOpacity for proper hit area on mobile.
Clean up 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' warnings (likely from ModalSheet/FormControls).

src/db/database.ts: Multi-statement execAsync schema may cause Error 21 in sqlite-wasm; recommend per-statement execAsync calls for portability.
src/context/AppDataContext.tsx: refresh() has no try/catch; a failure leaves UI in indeterminate state. Add error state + retry UI.
expo-sqlite installed version is 16.0.10 (matches package.json); the doctor warning about ~16.0.10 is benign.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: expo-sqlite 16.0.10 web worker (sqlite-wasm) throws SQLITE_MISUSE (code 21) during the initSchema/seedDefaultCategories phase of getDb(). Reproduction: (1) Open the public preview URL on a desktop browser viewport 390x844; (2) Wait for bundle to load; (3) Observe Expo red-screen overlay 'Uncaught Error — Error code 21: bad parameter or other API misuse' with stack node_modules/expo-sqlite/web/WorkerChannel.ts:64:25 -> WorkerMessageHandler -> Worker.addEventListener:argument_1 (SQLiteModule.ts:30). Likely cause: multi-statement execAsync block in initSchema (PRAGMA + multiple CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) is not handled atomically by sqlite-wasm worker, OR the 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON' executed prior to the CREATE TABLEs interacts badly with FOREIGN KEY refs. Mitigation tried: gating WAL pragma to native only — did not resolve. Recommended mitigation: split execAsync into per-statement execAsync calls, wrap each in try/catch, log failing SQL, and add a graceful error state in AppDataContext so the user sees a retry UI rather than Expo's dev red-screen.
